skill.name: pymc-bayesian-modeling
skill.description: Build, validate, diagnose, and compare Bayesian models with PyMC, ArviZ, MCMC sampling, variational inference, and reusable modeling templates.
skill.summary: Guides PyMC Bayesian modeling from model design through diagnostics, prediction, and comparison.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Bayesian modeling can be hard to structure, sample, diagnose, and compare. This skill provides PyMC workflows, templates, diagnostics, and model comparison guidance.
actual_capabilities: Guides standard PyMC workflows from data preparation to posterior prediction.
Provides examples for linear, logistic, hierarchical, Poisson, and time series models.
Explains MCMC, NUTS, ADVI, convergence checks, and posterior predictive checks.
Supports model comparison with LOO, WAIC, reliability checks, and model averaging.
Includes diagnostic script guidance for R-hat, ESS, divergences, plots, and reports.
Points users to reusable templates for linear regression and hierarchical models.
limitations: It does not fit models automatically without user data and a runnable Python environment.
It cannot guarantee statistical validity without domain review and data quality checks.
Large PyMC models may need significant CPU time, memory, or sampling tuning.
Included examples may need adaptation for PyMC version changes or project conventions.

use_cases.title: Estimate Uncertain Effects
use_cases.description: Build regression models that report posterior distributions and credible intervals instead of only point estimates.

use_cases.title: Analyze Grouped Data
use_cases.description: Create hierarchical models for grouped observations, partial pooling, and group-level uncertainty.

use_cases.title: Compare Candidate Models
use_cases.description: Use LOO, WAIC, diagnostics, and posterior checks to choose between competing Bayesian model specifications.

prompt_templates.title: Start a PyMC Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a PyMC model for this dataset and outcome. Identify predictors, likelihood, priors, and the first sampling plan.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Sampling Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my PyMC sampling diagnostics. Explain R-hat, ESS, divergences, tree depth, and practical fixes for this model.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Hierarchical Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this pooled model into a hierarchical PyMC model with non-centered parameterization and clear group-level summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Compare and Average Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these PyMC InferenceData results with LOO or WAIC, assess reliability, and suggest whether model averaging is appropriate.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a Bayesian linear regression workflow for standardized predictors and continuous outcomes.
output: A PyMC model plan with weakly informative priors and a normal likelihood.
A sampling plan with multiple chains, tuning, target acceptance, and a fixed random seed.
A validation checklist covering prior predictive checks, diagnostics, posterior predictive checks, and uncertainty reporting.

output_examples.input: A user has divergent transitions after fitting a hierarchical model.
output: A diagnosis that links divergences to difficult posterior geometry.
A recommended non-centered parameterization and a higher target acceptance value.
A follow-up checklist for R-hat, ESS, trace plots, and posterior predictive fit.

output_examples.input: A user wants to choose between three fitted PyMC models.
output: A model comparison plan using LOO or WAIC with log likelihood enabled.
Guidance for interpreting differences, standard errors, and Pareto-k reliability.
A recommendation on simpler models, refitting, or model averaging when results are close.

best_practices: Standardize predictors, use weakly informative priors, and run prior predictive checks before fitting.
Use multiple chains, fixed random seeds, and diagnostic thresholds before interpreting posterior estimates.
Compare models only after checking convergence, posterior predictive fit, and LOO or WAIC reliability.
anti_patterns: Do not interpret posterior estimates when R-hat, ESS, or divergence diagnostics are poor.
Do not use flat priors by default when weakly informative priors are available.
Do not choose a complex model only because its information criterion is slightly better.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build Bayesian models in PyMC, including regressions, hierarchical models, time series, diagnostics, and comparisons.

faq.question: Does it require Python experience?
faq.answer: Basic Python and statistics knowledge are helpful because the guidance uses PyMC, NumPy, and ArviZ concepts.

faq.question: Can it diagnose sampling problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains R-hat, effective sample size, divergences, tree depth, and common model reparameterization fixes.

faq.question: Does it include reusable templates?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill references templates for Bayesian linear regression and hierarchical or multilevel modeling workflows.

faq.question: Can it compare fitted models?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers LOO, WAIC, Pareto-k reliability checks, and model averaging for fitted PyMC models.

faq.question: Will it make my model statistically valid?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance, but model assumptions, priors, and conclusions still need expert review.
